facts.fact: L'Union reports the 196 km Fougamou-Mouila section (Ngounie province), built and pre-financed by Moov Africa Gabon Telecom, now connects Fougamou and Mouila to the national backbone; it is the first segment of phase 1 of the extension, ceded to the State by a convention signed at Mouila (dated 'yesterday' in a 7 Oct 2026 article).
GabonReview reports the national backbone in operation at 1,782 km of fibre, with a state official citing about 2,000 km today; places not listed.

GabonReview reports SPIN signed a 20-year concession with Gabon Fiber S.A. on 14 Sep 2026 under which Gabon Fiber will finance and build 1,651 km more (over 41 billion CFA francs), in three phases starting with Lambarene-Mouila-Tchibanga and Lalara-Makokou-Okondja, taking the network from 1,782 to 3,433 km.
GabonReview reports Gabon Fiber, concessionaire of the backbone, will operate exclusively on the wholesale market and not compete with telecom operators and ISPs; it will market capacity.

facts.fact: SPIN says GABON FIBER S.A. takes over operation of the 1,782 km of existing National Backbone (Backbone National Gabonais) when the current Axione Gabon delegation ends in November 2026.

SPIN says it and GABON FIBER S.A. signed a 20-year partnership on 14 September 2026 under which the concessionaire finances and builds 1,651 km of extensions in three phases, taking the network to 3,433 km.
SPIN says GABON FIBER S.A. is wholesale-only and that access to the backbone's capacity and services will be on transparent, fair and non-discriminatory terms for operators and ISPs.

SPIN's director-general says SPIN operates a fibre backbone from Libreville along the Transgabonais railway to Franceville, on to Bakoumba and Makokou and up to Cameroon via Booue, about 2,000 km in all, with two of the nine provinces not yet connected.
